title: CLQT: A Closed-Loop, Cost-Aware, Strategy-Consistent Benchmark for Diagnostic Evaluation of LLM Portfolio-Management Agents

p.t: Recent benchmarks for LLM-driven trading have advanced from static financial QA toward sequential decision-making [1,2,3]. Yet two gaps persist. The first is methodological coverage: no existing benchmark simultaneously enforces point-in-time data semantics, models realistic transaction and financing costs across asset classes, evaluates portfolio-level (not per-asset) decisions, measures strategy consistency across rounds, accumulates structured multi-tier memory, and treats tool orchestration as a benchmarkable capability. An agent that achieves high returns by inadvertently accessing future data, ignoring execution costs, or drifting from its mandate provides no credible signal about LLM capability. The second gap is interpretive, and it is the one this version foregrounds. The dominant evaluation idiom in LLM trading is the leaderboard: rank agents by Sharpe or cumulative return on a fixed period. But a leaderboard answers the wrong question for a research benchmark. A single quarter's return is dominated by the realized market path and by which risk profile happened to suit it; a model can top the table for reasons unrelated to the quality of its reasoning. More fundamentally, a credible ranking of models would require testing dozens of models across many regimes and repeated runs -far beyond the scope of any single paper. We therefore argue that the durable contribution of a closed-loop benchmark is not a ranking but a diagnostic instrument: an apparatus that reads an agent's full decision trail and localizes where in the gather→analyze→decide→execute→reflect loop, and why, the process breaks down.

CLQT is built to be that instrument. Its design thesis is: a model should be called "superior" only when there is evidence of dominance across the relevant capability axes, and consistently across sub-periods -a bar that, by construction, is rarely met cleanly, which is exactly the point. The value the benchmark delivers is the map of limitations it produces, reusable as the model panel grows. To make the map concrete we introduce a five-axis diagnostic capability scorecard computed entirely from the audit trail ( §6.4), and we render the trail trustworthy with a tamper-evident hash chain that any third party can recompute ( §4.4). Figure 1 summarizes the design as a whole. The contributions of this paper are: 1. A diagnostic reframing of closed-loop trading evaluation: the contribution is an instrument that maps agent limitations, with an explicit standard ("consistent dominance across axes and sub-periods") that resists premature ranking. 2. A five-axis capability scorecard (APM-CS) -Coherence, Acuity, Composure, Discipline, Reliability -each a finance instantiation of a general agent-evaluation capability, synthesized from existing audit fields with no new instrumentation. 3. A held-out LLM-as-judge for the Coherence axis (non-cohort, reasoning-enabled, cached), guarding against self-preference bias -with the headline coherence gap corroborated by a second, different-family held-out judge (Spearman ρ = 0.65), so the finding is not an artifact of one judge. 4. A tamper-evident audit hash chain: each round's observation and action hashes are recomputed on verification and linked to the prior round's action hash, so any post-hoc edit to a stored decision is detectable. 5. A closed-loop benchmark substrate with strict temporal integrity, institutional cost modeling, strategy-consistency measurement, three-tier memory, 19 MCP tools, mandate-aware synthesis, 3-D scouting, intertemporal sentiment trajectories, and verified live broker execution (carried forward and consolidated from prior versions). 6. A grounded demonstration: a chain-verified year-long bi-weekly campaign (5 models × 2 skill modes, repeated runs for the reliable models) plus a 13-configuration ablation grid (eight single-module / cost-tier variants and four multi-module cluster knockouts, repeated-run), a held-out Coherence judge, and a live broker trackshowing the instrument separates outcome from capability, surfaces model-specific limitations, and explicitly bounds what the evidence can claim.

Recent work (2025-2026), read closely. Four strands of very recent work each sharpen one facet of the problem; reading what each does and does not measure is the clearest way to locate CLQT. Full-pipeline scoring. PortBench [7] is the closest in spirit -it evaluates the entire portfolio-management pipeline with correlation-aware scoring and a cross-stage errorpropagation metric. But it scores that pipeline as a backtest over historical windows, stage-by-stage, rather than as a closed loop -without the persistent memory and tool use a live agent runs on. Its central move -decomposing where in the pipeline error originates rather than reporting a single score -is precisely the diagnostic stance CLQT adopts; CLQT extends it to a closed loop with memory, MCP tools, realistic costs and a live track ( §3, §5), and replaces stage-accuracy with a five-axis capability profile. Returns-centric autonomous trading. StockBench [1] and AI-Trader [3] run autonomous stock-trading agents end-to-end and report returns-centric outcomes (cumulative return, Sharpe, drawdown) rather than a decision-process capability profile. Their demonstration that capable models can trade profitably motivates CLQT's complementary questionis the profit coherent with the agent's stated reasoning? -which §7 shows it frequently is not (the Sharpe leader is a 5-of-26-round artifact).

A focused line documents the failure mode CLQT's TimeGate exists to prevent: Profit Mirage [8] shows that apparent LLM-agent alpha largely collapses once information leakage is removed, and memory-controlled masking [9] reports that returns under leakage-controlled evaluation are substantially explained by passive market and style exposure rather than stock-selection alpha. These results motivate CLQT's hard temporal gate ( §4) and per-run integrity ledger: we treat point-in-time enforcement as a precondition for a trustworthy number, not an optional safeguard. Memory as a measured variable. Memory-controlled trading benchmarks [9] ("from knowing to doing") isolate the variable CLQT promotes to a first-class axis -whether an agent can convert recalled experience into improved action -which CLQT measures directly through its three-tier memory ( §3.6) and the memory ablation ( §7.7).

No existing benchmark combines these facets. PortBench has the pipeline view but is backtest-only and not a closed loop; the returns benchmarks have autonomy and sometimes a live track but report a scalar; the integrity line fixes one precondition in isolation; the memory line isolates one variable. CLQT occupies the position none of them fills: a closed-loop, cost-aware, point-in-time, memory-and tool-bearing system that scores the decision process as a five-axis capability profile across both backtest and live (Table 1).

No cost-awareness. Prior benchmarks either ignore transaction costs [1,2,3,4] or apply a single flat commission [6]. CLQT implements four calibrated cost models ( §3.4) across four asset classes and four cost tiers, plus daily financing-cost accrual. No cross-round learning evaluation. InvestorBench [5] mentions memory but does not formalize or measure it. CLQT's three-tier memory ( §3.6) stores structured event-action-outcome records that decay and consolidate. No tool synthesis evaluation. AI-Trader [3] mandates tool-only execution but does not evaluate orchestration quality. CLQT logs every MCP tool call with hashes and latency.
All prior benchmarks treat news as single-round context. CLQT accumulates news across cycles in a persistent store ( §3.8) and measures whether agents reason about sentiment dynamics.

p.s: The LLM-Agent Infrastructure CLQT Builds On
p.t: Before it is a finance benchmark, CLQT is an LLM-agent system, and almost none of its machinery originates in financial AI -the loop, the memory, the tools, and the multi-agent committee are all adapted from the general agent-infrastructure literature of 2022-2025. We name that provenance explicitly, because it makes the design legible: each component exists to instantiate a mechanism that line of work showed to matter, and CLQT's contribution is to make that mechanism measurable in a cost-bearing, temporally-gated decision process. Reasoning-acting loop. The five-stage loop follows the reasoning-and-acting paradigm of ReAct [15] and the self-critique loop of Reflexion [16]. CoALA (Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents) [19] supplies the unifying frame -language agents as production systems with explicit memory, action, and decision modules -that CLQT's stage decomposition mirrors almost one-to-one (and connects directly to the ACT* grounding of §2.4).

p.s: Memory -borrowed from general agent infrastructure, not finance.
p.t: The intuition for CLQT's three-tier memory comes from outside trading entirely. Generative Agents [17] showed that a memory stream with periodic reflection and relevance-weighted retrieval yields coherent long-horizon behavior in a sandbox of simulated humans; MemGPT [18] reframed context management as operating-system-style paging between a working context and external stores; and CoALA [19] organizes agent memory into working, episodic, semantic, and procedural tiers. CLQT adapts exactly this lineage -a memory stream that consolidates event→action→outcome records, decays, and is retrieved by relevance -to a portfolio ledger, with extracted "lessons" as reusable procedural memory. The novelty is not the mechanism but treating "does recalled experience improve the next decision?" as a measured axis rather than an assumed benefit (memory ablation, §7.7)answering for trading the question memory-controlled benchmarks [9] pose in general.

That agents should act through tools rather than emit answers directly is the lesson of the tool-augmented-LLM line, exemplified by ToolLLM [21]; CLQT operationalizes it with a Model-Context-Protocol [20] tool layer (19 quantitative tools) -every tool call hashed, timed, and auditable, so tool use becomes evidence rather than a black box. Multi-agent committee and the structured scaffold. The role-decomposed committee (PM, Risk Officer, . . . ) draws on the general multi-agent-framework literature; the structured skill mode is inspired most directly by MetaGPT [22], whose central finding is that encoding standard operating procedures into the agent workflow reduces cascading error relative to free-form coordination. That result is the intuition behind CLQT's structuredvs-autonomous contrast ( §7.6): we do not assume scaffolding helps -we make the SOP-vs-autonomy trade-off an experimental variable and measure which models it helps, which it constrains, and on which axes. Within finance, the committee also builds on multi-agent trading frameworks like TradingAgents [10] and memory-augmented trading agents like FinMem [11]. Evaluation as a capability profile. The decision to report a profile rather than a scalar is itself borrowed: HELM [14] argued for holistic, multi-metric evaluation over a single leaderboard number, and agent benchmarks such as AgentBench [23] and τ -bench [24] score agents across tasks and trajectories rather than final answers. CLQT is the finance instantiation of that turn -five axes, a hash-chained audit trail, and a held-out judgespecialized to a closed-loop, cost-bearing portfolio process.

Evaluation methodology and judge design. Beyond the trading-benchmark literature, CLQT borrows from the broader practice of capability diagnostics in LLM/agent evalu-ation: reporting a profile of skills rather than a scalar, controlling for confounds with held-out judges and ablations, and being explicit about statistical power (repeated runs, confidence intervals, sensitivity of conclusions to setup). Recent work on LLM-as-judge [13] cautions about self-preference bias and the need for non-cohort judges and rubric grounding. CLQT instantiates these practices in finance: the five-axis scorecard is a capability profile; the Coherence judge is held out from the evaluated cohort; ablations and a repeated-run protocol bound module-importance claims; and reliability (format adherence, completion, truncation) is a first-class axis rather than an auxiliary note. This aligns with procedure-aware agent evaluation [12], which scores the correctness of the process rather than only task success. CLQT's held-out reasoning judge -cached, non-cohort, and reported alongside the mechanical signal-action agreement it systematically diverges from (the +0.33/+0.34 gap of §5.5) -is a finance instantiation of that stance: the divergence between the two, essentially the same on backtest and live, is itself the diagnostic. Architecturally, CLQT's role-decomposed committee and reflect-and-learn stage build on multi-agent financial frameworks like TradingAgents [10] and memory-augmented trading agents like FinMem [11], and follow the ReAct [15] / Reflexion [16] reasoning-acting-reflection paradigm; its three-tier memory connects to general agentic-memory work [18,19] and its tool layer to the MCP standard [20]. CLQT is complementary to broad financial-LLM benchmark suites in treating the decision process itself as a measurable capability profile.

CLQT's architecture is not ad hoc: each pillar instantiates an established model of decision-making or cognition, and several of the paper's findings are most naturally read through these lenses. We make the mappings explicit because they are what lets a trading benchmark speak to general agent behavior.

The gather→analyze→decide→execute→reflect loop is a finance instantiation of Boyd's OODA cycle (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act) [26] and of the classic three-level situation-awareness model -perception of task-relevant elements, comprehension of their meaning, and projection of their near-future implications. The mapping is direct: Intelligence Acquisition is perception, Signal Synthesis is comprehension, Portfolio Construction is projection-and-decision. This grounding also defines the Acuity axis ( §6.4): a Level-1 (perception) failure -attending to salient-butirrelevant cues -is exactly what Acuity measures when it contrasts an agent's response to informative signals against a volatility distractor. Reasoning vs. acting ←-Anderson's declarative/procedural distinction. Anderson's ACT* theory of cognition [25] separates declarative knowledge (factual propositions in semantic memory) from procedural knowledge (condition-action production rules compiled only through repeated practice). Anderson's central claim -that procedural skill is acquired by compiling declarative precursors through application, not by declarative retrieval alone -predicts a specific deficit in text-trained models: they encode the propositions of a strategy (declarative) but not the production rules that let those propositions govern an action (procedural), because the compilation step requires active practice a text corpus cannot supply. This is the theoretical basis for CLQT's central Coherence axis and, we argue in §8, the most parsimonious explanation of its headline finding -the systematic gap between what an agent states and what it does. Reflect-and-learn ←-experiential-learning theory. The Attribution & Lesson Extraction stage and three-tier memory operationalize an experiential-learning cycle (concrete experience → reflective observation → abstract conceptualization → active experimentation) and follow the ReAct [15] / Reflexion [16] reasoning-acting-reflection paradigm; the memory tiers themselves draw on the classic episodic/semantic distinction and recent agentic-memory work [18,19]. Reflection is, in Anderson's terms, the benchmark's attempt to supply the missing practice -and whether it helps is an empirical question the memory ablation ( §7.7) is built to answer.

Composure ←-behavioral finance. The Composure axis measures overreaction to volatility -the LLM-agent analogue of the classic overreaction hypothesis from behavioral finance and of noise-driven trading: a disciplined agent should not churn its book in response to transient volatility. Reading agent churn as overreaction connects CLQT's per-round turnover-vs-volatility regression to a long empirical tradition.

Grounding the five axes in cognition and decision theory is what makes them portable -the finance task is the instrument, but the capabilities it measures are not finance-specific, which is why a portfolio-management benchmark can function as a general agent diagnostic. We map each axis to its construct in §8.2.

CLQT operates as a five-stage closed loop executed by TradingEngine, which orchestrates Protocol modules through a six-agent architecture. The loop is the OODA / situation-awareness decision cycle of §2.4 made executable -perception (IA), comprehension (MSS), projection-and-decision (MAPC), action (COE), and reflection (ALE) -and the role decomposition follows the multi-agent financial-trading line [10] while the reflect-and-learn stage instantiates the ReAct [15] / Reflexion [16] paradigm. Each stage is a Python Protocol interface -implementations can be swapped without inheritance. All quantitative analysis is performed through 19 typed tools defined to the Model-Context-Protocol (MCP) standard and grouped into four namespaces (market-data, quant-tools, news-sentiment, execution); within the benchmark these run in-process against the underlying quant and data libraries -we adopt the MCP tooldefinition interface and schemas, not a networked server transport -so every analytical step is an auditable, schema-checked tool call rather than free-form text generation (full inventory in Appendix B, Table B1). The five stages are: 1. Intelligence Acquisition (IA) -gather market, news, macro, and asset-classspecific data; scout universe candidates. 2. Multi-Source Signal Synthesis (MSS) -produce signals, risk assessments, and factor decompositions. 3. Mandate-Aware Portfolio Construction (MAPC) -propose and validate target allocations against the investment mandate. 4. Cost-Optimal Order Execution (COE) -generate and execute orders with cost-minimizing strategies. 5. Attribution & Lesson Extraction (ALE) -attribute performance, extract structured lessons, update memory. The atomic unit of evaluation is the DecisionRound: DecisionRound: round_id, as_of_ts, run_id, model_id |-IA: market_snapshot, news_items, sentiment_trajectory, macro_indicators, | asset-class-data, candidate_signals |-MSS: signals, risk_report_pre, factor_attribution |-MAPC: portfolio_before, target_allocation, mapc_delta_proposed/projected, | mapc_adjustments_clipped, universe_changes, target_adherence |-COE: orders, execution_report, portfolio_after, financing_cost |-ALE: risk_report_post, reflection_notes, lessons_generated |-Memory: consistency_score, realized_pnl_this_round, memory_provenance |-Cost/IO: agent_costs[] (in/out/cache/reasoning tokens, elapsed_s, cost_usd) |-Reliab: decision_attempts, parse_failures `-Audit: observation_hash, action_hash, prev_round_hash, tool_calls_log, signed sentiment_trajectory, candidate_signals, the mapc_delta_ fields, agent_costs[], parse_failures, and prev_round_hash* are the fields the diagnostic scorecard ( §6.4) and the hash chain ( §4.4) read. Crucially, every metric in this paper is recoverable from this record -no new instrumentation was added to compute the scorecard.

CLQT employs a six-agent architecture where specialized agents receive agent skills -structured workflow protocols -that define the sequence of MCP tool calls and reasoning steps. Each agent (Research, Analyst, PM, Risk Officer, Execution, Reflection) maps onto a stage of the loop and is granted only the tool subset its role needs; this stage-to-agent-to-tool mapping is shown in Figure 2, and the exact skill files and tool assignments are available from the authors on request. Structured vs. Autonomous Skill Modes CLQT supports a skill rigidity ablation via agent.skill-mode: • structured: Six specialized agents with restricted tool subsets matching their stage role and prescribed skill protocols. Agents reason within the workflowformulating views, adjusting signal weights -but cannot change the workflow topology. A Risk Officer gate may reject and request a revision. • autonomous: A single AutonomousOrchestratorAgent owns the entire pipeline from SCOUT through REFLECT, receiving all tools and only a mandate document, constraint set, and required output schema. It decides which tools to call, in what order, how often, and whether to skip stages. Both modes use real agentic tool calling: LLM tool-use blocks are executed in-process against the actual quant and data libraries, with results fed back in a multi-turn loop. This is not simulated tool use or pre-assembled prompt data. (As §6.4/ §7 detail, this mode switch is a confound for two axes -Discipline and Acuity -that we control by comparing within mode.)

p.s: Multi-Source Information Gathering and 3-Dimensional SCOUT Stage
p.t: Standard Data Channels The IA stage gathers data from complementary sources, each enforced through the TimeGate ( §4.1) and each mapped to a backtest and a live provider so the two tracks see equivalent inputs (Table 2): 3-Dimensional SCOUT Stage Real universe candidates differ not only in momentum but in earnings quality and correlation structure with macroeconomic regimes. CLQT formalizes this through a 3-dimensional SCOUT stage inserted between IA and MSS. For every candidate-pool symbol not currently held, the stage computes, using data available as of as_of_ts: • Dimension 1 -Technical Momentum (m i ): 12-month minus 1-month price return. • Dimension 2 -Core Fundamentals (f i ): most recent earnings-surprise percentage (Finnhub/EDGAR), with analyst-consensus deviation as fallback. • Dimension 3 -Macro Correlation (ρ mkt i ): 60-day rolling Pearson correlation of daily log returns with SPY; a companion ρ rate i (vs. TLT) captures rate sensitivity. All three are z-scored cross-sectionally and combined: with a degenerate guard (correlation set to None and weight redistributed when the window has <10 observations or near-zero variance). The top-K candidates (default K = 5) are surfaced to MAPC and recorded in candidate_signals. The 50/30/20 split is an ablation default, not a derived optimum (ablation_scout_weights reserved). Figure 3 illustrates the ranking on a real campaign example (JNJ vs. FCX). A1). The cost tier is experiment-configurable (not hard-coded), enabling the cost-tier sensitivity ablation ( §7.7); the default is LOW, calibrated against the live broker paper fills ( §5.2).

CLQT computes a ConsistencyScore C t after each round: t = 0.25 • (1 -d style ) + 0.25 • τ consist + 0.25 • s adhere + 0.25 • a target capturing style drift, turnover consistency, signal adherence, and mandate alignment. When C t < 0.7 a drift warning is injected with a per-asset delta cap |δ i | ≤ δ/2. The components feed the Composure and Discipline axes ( §6.4); Figure 4 shows the four-component decomposition.

A three-tier memory architecture (Figure 5) accumulates and generalizes behavioral patterns across sessions: • Working memory: current observation pack plus the most recent N = 3 rounds. • Episodic memory: structured event-action-outcome records, decaying at α e = 0.95/round. • Semantic memory: generalized cross-asset patterns consolidated from episodic records, α s = 0.98. Every k = 12 rounds a consolidation pass merges episodic records sharing asset/event/outcome patterns. memory_provenance records which memories influenced each round, enabling the memory ablation ( §7.7). Decay is applied at retrieval time as α ∆round and contributes the recency term of the relevance score (alongside asset/event/regime overlap). The two rates are fixed defaults, not tuned against returns -they encode only the prior that specific episodic records should fade faster than generalized semantic patterns; α e = 0.95 and α s = 0.98 per round correspond to half-lives of ≈13.5 and ≈34 rounds, and the episodic rate is exposed as a config parameter for tuning or ablation.

The MAPC decision reconciles a quantitative optimizer proposal with the PM agent's tactical overlay through four layers: quantitative proposal (w opt ), budgetneutral agent overlay (δ with conviction scores), constrained projection onto the feasible set F, and Risk Officer validation with an execution gate. The agent's proposed overlay δ is recorded before projection as mapc_delta_proposed, and the projected result as mapc_delta_projected, with mapc_adjustments_clipped counting constraint clips. This separation is what lets the scorecard measure an agent's intent (Acuity, Coherence on proposed deltas) distinctly from the optimizer/MAPC machinery that may overwrite it.

The top-K SCOUT candidates are surfaced to the PM alongside current holdings, enabling agent-driven rotation, constrained by a per-round addition cap, a minimum holding-period guard, and the turnover budget. A post-parse cross-validation pass resolves logical contradictions.

p.s: Intertemporal Sentiment Trajectory and News Persistence
p.t: Prior work treats news as a point-in-time context. CLQT instead surfaces how sentiment is evolving. gather_news() uses a dynamic lookback L t = max(7, t as_oft last_rebalance + 1 day) and a persistent NewsStore that deduplicates and supplements articles across runs, so weekend or prior-round articles remain available within free-tier API limits. Articles are grouped into per-(symbol, day) SentimentDay objects (mean sentiment, count, most-extreme headline) forming a sentiment trajectory, classified IMPROVING/DETERIORATING/STABLE by comparing the last-3-day to first-3-day mean against δ thresh = 0.1. The PM receives a structured trajectory table (Figure 6); the trajectory is stored in DecisionRound.sentiment_trajectory for replay. The news-sentiment module ablation ( §7.7) toggles this channel.

All data access passes through TimeGate, enforcing ∀d ∈ D t : timestamp(d) ≤ t as_of . For live mode an intraday_cutoff freezes access N minutes before the decision timestamp. The TimeGate applies uniformly to all modalities, including memory retrieval and the NewsStore supplement pass.

Two complementary probes are implemented: canary documents (synthetic disclosures with unique identifiers detected via substring + fuzzy match) and future-shift leakage probes (paired baseline/probe decisions with normalized L1 weight divergence). These detection probes are part of the substrate but were not exercised in this single, benign campaign; contamination resistance here rests on the point-in-time gate and per-model cutoff filtering ( §4.2), the live post-cutoff track ( §5.5), and the verified hash chain ( §4.4). Active adversarial/canary probing to stress the capability axes directly is a hardening direction ( §8.8).

Each DecisionRound is sealed into a recompute-verifiable hash chain: a content hash over the inputs the agent saw and a content hash over the decision it took, with each round's hash folded into the next so the run forms an append-only ledger. Verification re-derives every hash from the persisted record and checks both that it matches the stored value and that the chain linkage holds; any post-hoc edit -a changed weight, a deleted order, a reordered round -breaks the chain at the first altered record. The audit trail is therefore tamper-evident: a reviewer handed only the persisted per-run store can independently confirm that the recorded decisions are exactly those the engine produced. Every campaign run passes chain verification end-to-end.

Rather than a single fixed period, CLQT assigns models to evaluation groups by training cutoff: Group B (cutoff > 2 years ago) → 2-year backtest from the cutoff; Group A (cutoff > 1 year ago) → 1-year backtest. Backtest parameters: 252-day warmup; configurable initial capital (default $1,000,000); bi-weekly rebalance (the 26-round campaign cadence, §7.2); LOW cost tier by default; deterministic given the configuration. In this paper's campaign every evaluated model's cutoff precedes the single 1-year window ( §7.2), so the longer 2-year Group B path, though supported, is not exercised by this cohort. Universe and starting book. The investable universe is derived from the S&P 100 -large, liquid, survivorship-controlled names with point-in-time membership (a symbol enters only once it was actually in the index as of the decision date). Each run opens from a core book of roughly 14 equal-weighted holdings carried as the starting portfolio, against a candidate pool of ~58 additional names (≈72 symbols in total) that the SCOUT stage ( §3.3) ranks for rotation. The universe is deliberately broad enough to permit meaningful selection and turnover, yet bounded so the cohort stays comparable across models and the news/fundamentals channels remain tractable within free-tier API limits.

A live track serves two purposes: (1) genuine contamination resistance -decisions execute on data that postdates every model's training cutoff -and (2) a check that the benchmark's execution abstractions map onto a real broker's order lifecycle. CLQT integrates a commercial broker's paper-trading API. Each session gathers and decides with the decision timestamp fixed to the Sunday before the Monday open, covering weekend news and matching the Monday backtest round's as-of time so the two tracks are comparable on identical data; it then previews and submits orders at the open, polls fills, reconciles the resulting book from the broker's positions and cash ledger, and locks the portfolio between rebalances. A dedicated execution agent optimizes only cost and fill quality -the target weights are fixed by the upstream decision. The live track thus executes real fills on genuinely unseen, post-cutoff data; the broker integration is documented and available from the authors on request.

CLQT distinguishes rebalancing (mechanical weight restoration) from re-optimization (full pipeline producing a new target) via three rebalance modes -calendar, threshold, and agent-discretion -enabling evaluation of when-to-trade judgment.

The two tracks are run on the same dates and configuration and reported on the same metric suite, so discrepancies are attributable: a backtest Sharpe exceeding live by more than ~0.2 flags possible contamination, while fill-price divergence between simulated and live execution gauges cost-model calibration.

The live track ran 2026-06-15 → 06-26 (nine valid NYSE days across two consecutive weeks) as a daily-rebalance campaign on a shared broker paper account: 6 newer "thinking" models (minimax-m3, deepseek-v4-pro, qwen3.7-plus, gpt-5.4-mini, gemini-3.5-flash, claude-sonnet-4.6) × {structured, autonomous} = 12 concurrent virtual-ledger sessions, each a $1M slice at medium reasoning. (2026-06-19, Juneteenth, is a NYSE holiday; that round priced on prior-session data and is dropped via a published exclusion manifest -an integrity detail enforced by an exchange-calendar gate.) Each ledger is pre-loaded with an equal-weight core book at the prior close, so only the daily delta reaches the broker; an end-of-day two-layer flatten returns the shared account to flat. Because the live cohort is a newer generation than the backtest cohort, and the account is flattened daily so realized P&L is a sequence of one-day deltas, we treat live returns as indicative-only and evaluate the live track at the decision level: does the instrument produce coherent, interpretable capability diagnostics on data the models never saw? The two-week horizon (nine rounds, up from a four-round week-1 pilot) is what lets the live axes resolve rather than merely sketch.

Computing the five axes over the nine valid rounds (Coherence via the same held-out judge; Acuity / Composure / Discipline / Reliability from the trail; Table 3) separates the live cohort along the same dimensions as backtest, and -as in backtest -no configuration dominates all five axes. claude-sonnet-4.6 leads (autonomous APM-CS 69.1, Coherence 0.57, Reliability 1.00), with qwen3.7-plus autonomous (61.8) and deepseek-v4-pro (≈60 in both modes) close behind; the scaffold again diverges by model -qwen3.7-plus and gpt-5.4-mini both score higher autonomous than structured (61.8 vs 41.8; 50.9 vs 47.3), while deepseek is mode-symmetric. Two model-specific signatures stand out and are diagnostically the most useful rows. minimax-m3 is the cohort's Reliability and Composure floor: it logs parse failures in both modes (Reliability 0.33 autonomous / 0.53 structured) and carries the cohort's steepest volatility-overreaction slope (≈1.0 → Composure 0.48), i.e. it churns its book hardest against transient volatility. gpt-5.4-mini is the other low-Composure pair (≈0.50). The autonomous-mode behavior behind minimax's reliability hit -a convergence to holdis dissected, together with gemini-3.5-flash's distinct hold mechanism, in §7.11. The cross-track invariant (headline live result). The mechanical signal-action agreement and the held-out reasoning judge -the two components of Coherence -differ by +0.33 on the backtest and +0.34 on the live track (backtest agreement 0.59 / judge 0.27; live agreement 0.61 / judge 0.27; Fig. 7 -unrounded cohort means give gaps of 0.326 and 0.339). Two different cohorts, two periods (a bi-weekly year vs nine live days), two cadences -yet effectively the same systematic gap between agreeing with signals mechanically and cohering with one's own stated reasoning. This is direct evidence that the instrument measures the same decision property on genuinely unseen data (not that any single model generalizes -see §8.7) -a claim a live track can support that a backtest cannot. Newer live models score somewhat higher on the judge than their backtest-era predecessors (e.g., deepseek 0.25 → 0.44), and agreement rises in step, so the difference stays pinned even as both levels lift. What the gap measures, and why coherence scores low. The two halves of Coherence ask different-difficulty questions. Agreement checks only the direction of each proposed trade against the sign of that name's informative composite -a low bar a coinflip clears at 0.5 and modest skill lifts to ~0.6. The judge asks whether the specific weights are a coherent consequence of the agent's own stated analysis -and the cohort fails it: across the campaign the held-out judge's mean score is 2.12 of 5 (mode 2; normalized 0.28). The gap is therefore not a quirk of one metric but the distance between two competencies -aligning with external signals versus keeping one's allocation consistent with one's own narrative. Reading the cached judge rationales, the low scores are concrete and checkable, recurring in five patterns: (i) direct contradiction ("analysis says TSLA should be reduced but its weight change is +1.7%"); (ii) equal-weight collapse that ignores the differentiation the analysis emphasized ("near-equal-weight 7.1-7.3% across all names . . . CAT +3.74 vs LIN -3.59 receive essentially identical weights, incoherent with a signal-driven meanvariance analysis"); (iii) name mismatch (the thesis names AVGO/GS/MS/NEM; the book holds PG/AMT/NEE/AMZN); (iv) weights anti-correlated with the cited signals (overweighting the most bearish name at 12% while the strongest bullish name gets 0.2%); and (v) no thesis at all (an autonomous→MAPC placeholder with "no thesis for the specific name selection"). This is the stating-versus-doing deficit made concrete.

Where the incoherence enters. Part of it is the agent's narrative not matching even its own intent; part is the machinery. The judge scores the post-construction target, which the quant optimizer and the constrained projection have already reshaped -so the equal-weight collapse (the optimizer flattening a tactical tilt) and the cap-hits (the projection clipping) are partly system effects, not pure reasoning failures. The instrument records proposed (pre-MAPC intent) separately from projected (post-machinery) precisely so the two can be attributed ( §3.7); the extreme tell is the bare-workflow agent ( §7.7) whose entire rationale is "Optimizer: risk_parity . . . Accepted 0 adjustments" -there is no thesis for the allocation to cohere with. Read at the level of the agent-in-the-system, then, the gap measures a real reasoning-action consistency deficit: a competent reader, handed the agent's analysis, would not derive the book it produced. What the cross-track agreement does and does not establish. That the gap reproduces on genuinely post-cutoff live data rules out memorization -a leakage artifact would shrink off-distribution, and it does not. More telling than the headline match is what moves versus what sticks: the component levels rise with model generation (newer live models judge higher, e.g. deepseek 0.25 → 0.44, and agreement rises too) while the difference stays pinned -agents narrate better and point better in proportion, leaving the gap generation-invariant, the signature ACT* ( §2.4) predicts.

We are deliberate about the limits, though: even over nine live rounds the two gaps are close, not identical (0.326 vs 0.339) -strong enough that the small-sample "fortunate rounding" caveat of the week-1 pilot no longer applies, but still consistent with the same value rather than a proof of equality; and because both tracks share the metric, the match is instrumentconsistency, a statement about the apparatus measuring stably. The strongest robustness check is therefore the second judge (below), which rules out a different failure modeone judge's idiosyncrasy -than the cross-track test does. Read together they make the deficit reproducible and judge-robust, with the intrinsic-limitation interpretation the most parsimonious reading rather than a settled result. What the cross-track does not claim. The live and backtest cohorts are different model versions, so this is instrument-consistency, not same-model generalization; familylevel traits reflect model and condition (e.g., gemini's newer version intermittently holds live, §7.11, where the older one was active in backtest). Two weeks of live data also revise two week-1 reads that four rounds could not settle: gemini-3.5-flash, the week-1 Composure floor, lifts to the cohort's highest Composure once its week-2 low-turnover stretch enters the volatility-overreaction regression -the floor is in fact minimax-m3 (and gpt-5.4-mini); and gpt-5.4-mini's scaffold edge reverses to favor autonomy. With nine rounds the Composure and Acuity axes resolve well enough to rank, though they remain the shortest-horizon axes and are read with more caution than Coherence, Reliability, and Discipline.

Robustness to the judge. Because the coherence gap is the instrument's strongest claim, we corroborate it with a second, different-family held-out judge (GLM-5.2, also non-cohort and reasoning-enabled; full protocol in §6.4.1). The two judges agree closely (597 shared rounds, Spearman ρ = 0.65, 97% within one point on the 1-5 rubric; GLM marginally more lenient, mean 2.30 vs 2.11), and the gap survives the swap -+0.28 (backtest) / +0.34 (live) under GLM, statistically indistinguishable from minimax-m3's +0.33 / +0.34 -so the divergence is a property of the allocations, not of one particular judge.

CLQT supports 12 ablation dimensions in three categories (Table 4). Module flags: newssentiment, world-macro, cost-modeling, advanced-quant, systematic-execution, reflection, memory, investment-target, asset-class-data. Config overrides: cost-tier ∈ {zero, low, medium, high}, rebalance-mode ∈ {calendar, threshold, agent-discretion}. Process autonomy: skill-mode ∈ {structured, autonomous}.

The instrument scores agents against a full passive suite that every run computes automatically: the index ETFs SPY (S&P 500 proxy) and IEF (7-10y Treasuries); a synthetic 60/40 (0.6•SPY + 0.4•IEF); an equal-weight portfolio of the agent's own investable universe (EW-Universe); and four algorithmic baselines -buy-and-hold, equal-weight (rebalanced), risk-parity (inverse-vol), and 12-1 momentum. For each, the run reports cumulative/excess return, information ratio, and tracking error. The headline question -does any agent beat the cap-weighted index net of costs? -is answered against this suite, not a single benchmark.

The instrument records a broad metric suite -performance, benchmark-relative, cost, governance, consistency, learning, efficiency, reliability, and integrity -all recoverable from the audit trail (Table 5).

The scorecard is the instrument's read-out. It scores five capability axes from the audit trail, ordered high→low by how fundamental they are to competent autonomous portfolio management. Each axis is a finance instantiation of a general agent-evaluation capability, so a finding about a trading agent generalizes to a statement about the model's reasoning. Outcome (returns) is not an axis -it is a result explained by the axes. ① Coherence -general capability: global, systems-level reasoning vs. local greedy pattern-matching; an analogue of systematic alignment vs. turn-by-turn instructionfollowing at the level of reasoning (does the conclusion follow from the agent's own analysis?). Finance: the chosen allocation follows from the agent's stated research and the signals it cited. Synthesis: where A sig is signal-action agreement: the fraction of the agent's proposed trades (mapc_delta_proposed, pre-MAPC) whose direction matches the sign of that name's cross-sectional informative composite (below). J judge is the held-out LLM judge's score ( §6.4.1), normalized to [0,1]. Reveals shallow or self-contradictory reasoning that returns hide. ② Acuity (information attention / acuteness) -general: salience attention vs. distraction, i.e. endurance under polluted / misleading context. Finance: attend to informative signals amid a large noisy universe and a flood of news. Synthesis, on proposed adjustments (not final weights, which are confounded by the optimizer/MAPC): where ρ s is Spearman correlation, I = z(m 12-1 ) + z(e surp ) + z(n sent ) is the informative composite, and N = z(σ realized ) is the volatility-noise distractor. Each term is z-scored cross-sectionally per round and averaged over rounds with ≥3 proposed trades. Positive ⇒ the agent's intent tracks alpha-bearing signals more than the high-variance, low-alpha distractor; near-zero or negative ⇒ chasing noise.

③ Composure -general: robustness / consistency under input perturbation vs. reactive overcorrection. Finance: respond to volatility and misleading data with discipline, not churn. Synthesis (the mean of its legs, not a product): where s react is the (squashed, non-negative) regression coefficient of per-round one-way turnover on a market-volatility proxy (cross-sectional mean realized_vol), and c cons is the strategy-consistency leg when available; a high slope means turnover rises sharply with volatility. We score Composure as the average of its legs rather than their product for two reasons made concrete by the campaign: a product lets one weak leg collapse the whole axis (it sent a single model's Composure to ~0), and -because the strategy-consistency leg is produced by the memory module -a product made Composure uncomputable under the memory ablation ( §7.7). The mean is robust to a single low leg and falls back to the memory-free calm leg when consistency is absent, so Composure is defined for every configuration including memory-off ablations. (Style-drift is ≈0 cohort-wide, so it is reported separately rather than carried as a non-discriminating leg.) Reveals models that overreact to volatile or misleading inputs. ④ Discipline -general: systematic alignment to a standing mandate vs. turn-by-turn instruction-following -does the agent self-regulate to a policy even absent a hard guardrail? Finance: respect caps/turnover/risk budgets without relying on the MAPC clip. Synthesis (bounded to [0, 1]):

where r self is the self-constrained rate: the fraction of rounds whose target satisfies constraints pre-MAPC. d clip = min(1, āclip /κ) is clip dependence, measuring reliance on the reconciler to force the book inside the mandate (κ = 10, a fully-saturated structured round; āclip is the mean number of clipped MAPC adjustments). Both legs lie in [0, 1], so Discipline does too. (A turnover-cap leg used in earlier drafts was dropped: campaign turnover ~0.15 sits far below any real cap, so the leg was a non-discriminating constant.) Mode confound: RO-approval is meaningful only in structured; autonomous sets risk_approved=True by construction -so Discipline is compared within mode. ⑤ Reliability -general: protocol/format adherence + operational robustness + efficiency -the analogue of an agent completing a tool-use task in valid form, every time, at reasonable cost. Finance: close the loop in valid schema at acceptable compute. Synthesis: where r complete is completion rate, r parse is parse-fail rate, and r trunc is truncation rate. Efficiency is reported beside it ($/round, reasoning-tokens/round, latency).

Each axis is mapped to a cohort percentile and the five form a radar fingerprint (Figure 8); Table 6 tabulates the percentile profile and a composite APM-CS (mean of the five percentiles); pairwise dominance and win-rate across (axis × sub-period × run) with rank-stability (Kendall's τ ) are a planned broader-run output ( §8.8). The thesis bar -superior = consistent dominance across axes and sub-periods -is operationalized as: a configuration must win the large majority of axes against all rivals and hold that pattern across regime sub-periods and runs. The mode-confounded axes (②④) are flagged and compared within mode. Because each axis is a within-cohort percentile, APM-CS is a cohort-relative composite -adding or removing configurations rescales it, so cross-paper or expanded-panel comparison requires recomputation; the raw per-axis values (D1-D5) are the portable invariant.

The judge component of Coherence is scored by a held-out, non-cohort model -i.e. a model not in the evaluated setto avoid the self-preference bias documented for LLM-as-judge. For each round the judge receives a compact, audit-derived prompt: the agent's stated analysis (research brief and/or optimizer rationale), the top names by informative-composite strength with their underlying signals, the chosen target weights, and the proposed weight changes. It returns a 1-5 score for the single question "does the chosen allocation follow coherently from the stated analysis and signals?" -explicitly told to ignore profitability and to penalize self-contradiction and untethered allocations. Scores are cached by round_id (so re-runs never re-bill) and reasoning is enabled on the judge model deliberately: coherence adjudication is nuanced and the held-out judge is a reasoning model, so we trade a few cents per round for adjudication quality. Bumping the prompt version invalidates the cache so all rounds are re-judged consistently when the rubric changes. Two-judge protocol (primary + corroboration). The primary judge is minimax-m3 -it produces every Coherence number reported in §7 and §5. Because the agreement↔judge coherence gap ( §5.5) is the instrument's strongest claim, we corroborate it with a second, different-family held-out judge, GLM-5.2 (also non-cohort and reasoning-enabled), scored into a separate cache over the same rounds. The two judges agree closely at the round level (Spearman ρ = 0.65, 97 % within one point on the 1-5 rubric) and the gap reproduces under the swap ( §8.7), so the headline finding is a property of the allocations, not of one judge. Both judges are non-cohort; the second is used only as a robustness check, not blended into the primary score.

The same audit trail that powers the quantitative scorecard ( §6.4) also supports a qualitative, behavioral read -extracting each model's decision behaviors, stated reasoning, and recurring patterns into a human-legible picture of its "decision personality." This is the tradition of work that probes LLM black boxes through their observable actions and self-reports rather than their weights, and CLQT is unusually well-suited to it because every round is a complete, hash-chained, verifiable record ( §4.4). Captured per round, per model × mode, with no new instrumentation (the exact audit fields behind each are mapped in Appendix D, Table D1): • Stated reasoning -the agent's own narrative account of why an allocation was chosen: research and analyst briefs, the allocation rationale, risk-officer notes, and the post-round reflection. • Metacognition and learning -how a model abstracts experience into typed, reusable "lessons", and whether those lessons are later retrieved back into context. • Intent vs. guardrails -the gap between what the model proposed and what the reconciler allowed (in a sampled structured run the agent proposed 12-14 weight moves per round and 7-12 were clipped -a quantifiable "intent meets institutional guardrails" signal). • Inter-agent dynamics -how the PM and Risk Officer negotiate, and when the committee overrides itself. • Information foraging -each model's characteristic data-gathering strategy: which tools it calls, in what order, and how widely it explores the candidate universe.

• Cognitive effort -where a model "thinks hardest" (reasoning-token and latency budget per role) and whether that effort tracks decision quality. • Struggle signatures -where and why a model fails to produce a valid decision: retry loops, parse failures, and constraint violations. Method. Thematic coding of the reasoning corpus (optionally LLM-assisted via a held-out summarizer mirroring the judge protocol in §6.4.1), frequency analysis of intent-vs-clip and committee overrides, per-model tool-use fingerprints, lesson formation and reuse, and illustrative anecdotes -each tied to a hash-verified round so it is reproducible. Scope (honest caveat). We analyze stated and observable reasoning artifacts and behavioral metadata, not raw hidden chain-of-thought: providers generally do not return the thinking trace, and we persist reasoning-token counts, not the trace text. The interpretability is therefore of behavior + self-report -auditable and reproducible (every claim pinned to a hash-chained round), but situated one layer above the model's hidden cognition. We treat this scoping as a feature, not a gap: it keeps the "human reading of the AI" grounded in verifiable evidence rather than unfalsifiable introspection.

The experiments here are the full 1-year campaign -still not a model ranking, but a map of limitations across a 5-model cohort. The purpose is to show that the five-axis scorecard discriminates decision quality where outcome metrics conflate it, surfaces model-specific failures invisible to returns, and -by the instrument's own standard (consistent dominance across axes and sub-periods) -resists premature ranking even with repeated-run evidence. Rows report means over repeated runs; bootstrapped CIs and Kendall-τ rank-stability are a planned broader-run pass ( §8.8). The method, the axes, and the audit machinery are the contribution.

• RQ1 (instrument validity): Does the scorecard discriminate decision quality where outcome metrics conflate it? • RQ2 (capability ̸ = outcome): Is the Sharpe leader the capability leader, and does any single configuration dominate all five axes? • RQ3 (model-specific limitations): Does the audit trail surface model-specific failures invisible to returns? • RQ4 (scaffold effect): How does the structured↔autonomous skill mode shape the capability profile? • RQ5 (module importance): Do single-run module ablations yield clean importance claims, or is the repeated-run campaign required? • RQ6 (cost realism): Are the cost tiers calibrated, and how sensitive are conclusions to them? • RQ7 (passive comparison): Net of costs, does any agent beat the cap-weighted index and the broader passive suite?

Campaign grid. Five models spanning families, sizes, and reasoning styles -qwen3-235b (large MoE, non-thinking), gemini-2.5-flash-lite (small), deepseek-chat-v3.1 (mid, hybrid→non-thinking), gpt-5-mini (reasoning, effort low), claude-haiku-4.5 (small, thinking off) -each in structured and autonomous skill modes, repeated runs each for the three structurally-reliable models (means over runs; haiku and qwen3-235b single-run, qwen3 partial). Period: 26 bi-weekly rounds, 2025-06-16 → 2026-06-12; S&P-100-derived universe (14 core + 58 candidate = 72), all modules enabled, LOW cost tier, initial NAV $1M, context capped 32k for cohort comparability, uniform output budget 8192. Coherence judge: held-out, non-cohort minimax-m3, reasoning enabled, cached. Cutoff safety. Every model's training cutoff precedes the 2025-06-16 start (gemini Jan'25, gpt-5-mini May'24, claude-haiku Feb'25, deepseek Mar'25); qwen3 (Jun'25) sits within a documented ≤1-month grace. The IntegrityChecker records cutoff compliance per run. Ablation grid. Single anchor = gemini-2.5-flash-lite, structured, LOW (cheap; its structured runs complete): six module-off variants (cost-modeling, memory, reflection, newssentiment, world-macro, advanced-quant) + two cost-tier variants (medium, high) -8/8 runs complete via run_ablation.py ( §7.7, Figure 10). Parsing hardening. Before the campaign, the PM/Risk schema parsers were hardened to drop null list items (and lift bare-string items) in adjustments/checks -small models (notably gemini in structured mode) emit {"adjustments": [null, . . . ]}, which previously failed validation and degraded the round. This recovers the valid content and materially improves structured Reliability across the cohort ( §7.5). ★ qwen3-235b structured is reported on its completed rounds only -it never finishes more than a fraction of the campaign across its runs (a small, self-selected slice of rounds; see §7.5), versus a near-complete autonomous run. We trace the cause to operational, not cognitive, limits ( §7.5): at a 2048-token output cap the structured-schema JSON is truncated mid-answer, and at 8192 (truncation fixed) the model is throttled by provider rate-limiting (429→null) under the ~400-call load of a 26-round run. A 2-round smoke at 8192 completes cleanly with valid allocations, so the model can drive the pipeline -it cannot sustain it via this gateway. Its structured Sharpe (9.82) / beat (8/8) are therefore on a 5-round self-selected window and are meaningless except as a foil -read them only against its Reliability (~0.2). The autonomous run (25/26) is the trustworthy qwen3 row.

• F1 -Capability leader ̸ = outcome leader (the thesis, in one table). deepseek•structured tops APM-CS (72.4) with the most balanced profile (best Acuity 0.18, Discipline 0.90, Reliability 0.99) -yet it is mid-pack on Sharpe (2.96). The nominal Sharpe "winner" is qwen3•structured at an implausible 9.82 / beat 8-of-8 -but on 5/26 rounds with Reliability 0.19, the lowest APM-CS in the cohort (30.5): the scorecard flags it as a self-selected-window artifact, not a strategy. Among reliable configs the Sharpe leaders are haiku•structured (3.20) and deepseek•structured (2.96) -but haiku posts the lowest Coherence (0.15)its allocations do not follow its own stated analysis. A leaderboard would crown qwen3 (a spurious 5-round Sharpe); the scorecard instead returns a profile per config and explains why the headline number misleads (Figure 8, Figure 14). • F2 -Scaffold lifts capability for every model, by very different amounts. APM-CS structured vs autonomous: deepseek 72.4 → 36.7 (a 36-point swing), haiku 67.9 → 55.9, gpt-5-mini 57.8 → 54.9, gemini 45.0 → 38.8 -structured is higher for all four multi-mode models, but the lift ranges from ~3 points (gpt-5-mini) to 36 (deepseek). (qwen3's structured row is only 5 reliable rounds, so its mode contrast is uninformative.) Structured also broadly raises Composure (D3 mean 0.93 vs 0.88) and self-constraint (D4). So structure helps every model's capability profile, but by very different amounts -a statement only a multi-axis read makes (D2/D4 mode-confounded, compared within mode).

• F3 -Reliability deficits hidden by returns. gemini•structured posts a healthy +24.9% / Sharpe 2.26 yet Reliability 0.61 -residual schema parse-fails persist even with retries=3. qwen3•structured completes only 5/26 rounds (Reliability 0.19) -null/empty PM responses on the rest from output truncation and provider rate-limiting (operational, not cognitive; §7.5) -yet its 5 surviving rounds look spectacular. Both deficits are invisible to a returns-only view and are exactly what the D5 axis surfaces (Figure 9). The two have different causes -gemini's is genuine schema-adherence, qwen3's is infrastructure -which only the audit trail distinguishes. • F4 -Acuity is weak cohort-wide. D2 sits at 0.06-0.18 for the reliable configs, and both qwen3 modes are negative (-0.25 autonomous, -0.37 structured)their proposed trades track the volatility distractor more than the alpha-bearing composite. Even the best (deepseek•structured, 0.18) attends only modestly to the informative signals amid the noisy 72-name universe. • F5 -Net of realistic costs, agents clear some of the passive suite, not the index cleanly. Reliable structured runs beat a median ~6/8 baselines (deepseek 6.3, haiku 6.0, gemini 5.7), but the beaten set is dominated by bonds / risk-parity / EW / 60-40; autonomous runs beat far fewer (gemini and haiku autonomous: 1/8). (qwen3•structured's 8/8 is on 5 rounds -discount it.) The instrument scores against the whole suite, so "beats N/8" is honest rather than cherry-picked.

Methodology note. max_decision_retries was raised 1→3 mid-campaign after gemini's residual schema-unreliability caused ~16% optimizer-fallback rounds; retries=3 cuts that to ~0 without masking the Reliability axis (D5 still records per-attempt failures). The live timeout/decide budgets were likewise widened for the reasoning-heavy models. All campaign runs use retries=3.

The cross-model APM-CS radar (Figure 8), the single-and multi-module ablation ∆ grid on the gemini anchor ( §7.7, Figure 10), and the efficiency / cost-of-intelligence Pareto (Figure 14) are complete. Pairwise dominance / win-rate, the regime-stratified facet (risk-on / neutral / risk-off), and bootstrapped CIs / Kendall-τ rank-stability remain future passes ( §8.8).

The five-axis radar (Figure 8), split into structured (left) and autonomous (right) panels, visualizes the §7.3 finding that no configuration encloses all five axes. deepseek•structured is the most balanced enclosure (the APM-CS leader, 72.4) but does not top Coherence; the high-Sharpe configs (qwen3•structured, haiku•structured) are uneven -strong on one or two axes, collapsed on another (qwen3 on Reliability, haiku on Coherence); and the autonomous envelopes (right) are systematically smaller than their structured counterparts (left) for the same model. Capability is a shape, not a scalar -which is the whole point of refusing a single ranking.

Reliability is the axis that most cleanly separates the cohort -and it is invisible to returns. Three configurations carry reliability deficits -two are genuine governanceschema failures (gemini, deepseek-autonomous) and one is operational (qwen3) -each surfaced only by the audit trail's parse_failures / decision_attempts / completion fields: • qwen3-235b • structured is the reliability floor -but operationally, not cognitively. It completes only 4-8 of 26 rounds across three configurations (r1 5/26, r2 8/26, r3 4/26; Reliability ≈0.2), yet the audit trail attributes the cause to infrastructure, not portfolio reasoning. At a 2048-token output cap its structuredschema JSON is truncated mid-answer (21 of 465 calls hit the cap on the 72-name universe); raising the cap to 8192 eliminates truncation but exposes a second limit -the model is throttled by provider rate-limiting (≈200-500 429s per run → null responses) under the ~400-call load of a full campaign, isolated or concurrent alike. Decisively, a 2-round smoke at 8192 completes cleanly with valid allocations, so the model can produce a structured decision -it cannot sustain the call volume through this gateway. We therefore report qwen3•structured only as a reliability/operational case study, not a capability row: its 9.82 Sharpe on 5 self-selected rounds is precisely the spurious number the scorecard exists to expose. (It runs fine in autonomous, 25/26.) • gemini-2.5-flash-lite • structured posts a healthy +24.9% / Sharpe 2.26 yet Reliability 0.61 -residual parse-failures (~10/26 rounds on at least one attempt) persist across all its runs even with retries enabled. Retries recover the round, but the per-attempt schema failures are still recorded (as they must be) -strong outcome, measurable reliability deficit.

• deepseek-chat-v3.1 • autonomous inverts the pattern: excellent under the scaffold (structured Reliability 0.99) but 0.60 autonomous -the same model is reliable with the staged hand-off and substantially less reliable without it. By contrast gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 are schema-clean in both modes (Reliability ≈ 1.0). So governance-schema adherence is a real, model × mode-specific capability limit -the smaller models cannot reliably emit the structured decision -that a returns-only view misses entirely (gemini•structured beats ~6/8 baselines while failing the schema). This is precisely the kind of finding the instrument exists to produce, now robust across repeated runs rather than a single pilot run.

p.s: RQ4: Scaffold Shapes the Capability Profile
p.t: The skill mode reshapes the capability profile, and by markedly different amounts per model ( §7.3-F2). Structured raises APM-CS for every model -most dramatically deepseek (72.4 vs 36.7 autonomous, +36 points), then haiku (67.9 vs 55.9), more modestly gpt-5-mini (57.8 vs 54.9) and gemini (45.0 vs 38.8); qwen3's structured row (30.5) rests on only 5 reliable rounds, so its mode contrast is uninformative. It also broadly lifts Composure (D3): structured configs hold one-way turnover flat in volatility (D3 ≈ 0.92-0.95), and the autonomous configs sit slightly lower (D3 ≈ 0.79-0.92), with gemini•autonomous the lowest at 0.79 -the one configuration with a positive volatilityoverreaction slope (the others' is ≈0). Handing that model full autonomy makes it overreact to volatility -a stability cost the scaffold suppresses, and one the headline Sharpe hides. (Acuity② and Discipline④ are mode-confounded and compared within mode; the scaffold's Discipline gain shows up as higher D4 for the structured configs, ≈0.71-1.00 vs autonomous ≈0.45-0.65.) On Coherence. The held-out judge exposes a weakness the agreement proxy alone would miss. Signal-action agreement is middling-to-fine cohort-wide (~0.53-0.65), but the reasoning-enabled minimax-m3 judge scores the allocations' coherence low, so D1 sits in a 0.38-0.48 band for most configs -with claude-haiku•structured the outlier at 0.15: it posts the cohort's best reliable Sharpe (3.20) yet its allocations least follow its own stated analysis. The two Coherence components disagree -agents trade in broadly the right direction on average, but their narratives do not justify the specific weights -and that disagreement is the diagnostic, visible only because Coherence pairs a mechanical agreement check with an independent reasoning-capable judge; either alone would mislead. Readings. (i) Pipeline validated -all module-off runs (six variants, repeated) plus the two cost-tier variants completed 26/26 with ∆ computed against the verified baseline (Table 7). (ii) Cost realism (RQ6). The HIGH (Almgren-Chriss [27]) tier is miscalibrated -it charges ≈527 bps/round (~5.3%/round → -75% cumulative, Sharpe -1.06), an implausible drag confirming the decision to keep LOW and flagging a costmodel recalibration task; MEDIUM moves cost negligibly, so its -0.19 ∆Sharpe is decision noise. (iii) Module importance is not rankable by Sharpe -even across repeated runs. Every module-off ∆Sharpe is positive (means +0.09. . . +0.66) -removing a module never cleanly hurts, which is mechanistically implausible -and every run range straddles or sits inside the ±0.42 band, so none is separable; the extra runs narrowed the estimates without changing the verdict. no-world-macro (mean +0.66, range [+0.33, +1.06]) is the clearest favorable draw, not "macro helps." Returns variance dominates the module signal, and more runs will not fix what is a wrong-axis problem. (iv) The capability scorecard catches what Sharpe cannot. Removing the information stack leaves Sharpe in the noise yet collapses Acuity to ≈0.02 (the analysis-blind cluster, below) -the agent has no informative signals left to attend to, a capability loss invisible to returns. Removing memory is subtler: it strips Composure's strategy-consistency leg (the consistency_score only the memory module produces), so the axis falls back to its volatility-overreaction leg -under the old multiplicative Composure this made the axis uncomputable, a construct defect the v2 revision fixes ( §6.4); under v2 the dependency surfaces as the loss of the consistency leg rather than an undefined axis (and, because that leg sat below the calm leg in this benign window, the composite does not fall -the signal is the absent leg, read from the trail, not a lower number). So the ablation yields two robust signals -HIGH-tier mis-calibration (cost realism) and analysis-blind→Acuity (a capability dependency) -and a clean methodological result: module value is a multi-axis question that a returns-only ablation cannot answer, which is the entire reason the instrument scores five axes rather than one.

A single-module ablation cannot see combined contribution -modules may be individually redundant (the agent compensates when one input is gone) yet collectively essential. We therefore knock out whole capability clusters across repeated runs (12 more runs, all 26/26, same gemini anchor; the bare-workflow agent matches the full agent on returns Table 8. Multi-module (cluster) ablation: ∆Sharpe vs. the structured-gemini baseline (Sharpe 2.26) when an entire capability cluster is removed (12 runs, all 26/26 rounds, same gemini anchor). Run range is the min-max across repeated runs; Reading names the capability axis the knockout most implicates. All four clusters stay inside the ±0.42 repeated-run band on returns, yet the capability axes register what returns hide (analysis-blind → Acuity 0.02). (v) Combined removal does not separate on returns either, but the bare-workflow result is the striking case. None of the four cluster knockouts clears the ±0.42 band, and every ∆Sharpe is again positive (+0.16. . . +0.53), so even removing an entire capability cluster never cleanly hurts. The extreme case is G4 bare-workflow: with no information modules, no learning, and even the quant-optimization engine removed -the LLM sets the weights itself under the mandate, with a risk-parity execution fallback -it is statistically indistinguishable from the fully-augmented six-module agent on returns (∆Sharpe +0.26, range [-0.40, +0.66]; +27.3% vs the baseline's +24.9%). On this benchmark and period, the agentic scaffolding the system layers on contributes little to Sharpe. Yet -exactly as for the single-module grid -the capability axes register what returns hide: analysis-blind drives Acuity to 0.02 (the agent has no informative signals left to attend to), and both memory-removing clusters strip Composure's strategy-consistency leg (the axis stays computable via its memory-free fallback, §6.4). The interaction test thus confirms, more forcefully, the thesis: module value cannot be read off returns -not single-module, not cluster-level, not even against a stripped-to-the-mandate baseline -but the multi-axis scorecard does record what each removal costs. (That a bare LLM matches the scaffolded agent on returns while differing in capability is itself a finding the instrument exists to surface, and a caution against assuming added modules buy performance.)

That no ablation moves Sharpe is not the end of the story but the start of it: a returns-only read would call all thirteen configurations equivalent when they in fact differ sharply on risk, cost, and -most of all -decision behavior. We diagnose each, because this is exactly the discrimination the instrument exists to provide. (vi) The full performance profile (Table 9) -three facts Sharpe hides. (a) Genuine risk-adjusted skill, against the right benchmark: the full agent runs lower volatility (11.0% vs SPY's 11.9%) and half the drawdown (-4.1% vs -8.9%) at the same Sharpe (2.26 vs 2.29) and ≈2× the Calmar; its negative IR vs SPY (-0.04) is deliberate de-risking (giving up ~2.4% bull-market upside to halve the downside), an edge that inverts in a drawdown, not absence of skill. (b) That risk discipline is robust to ablation -every config but the mis-calibrated HIGH tier holds drawdown to -3.2. . . -4.7% and Calmar 5.8-8.7, with zero constraint-violations and style-drift across all thirteen -so it comes from the constrained closed-loop (caps + staged Risk-Officer/MAPC), not the optional modules. (c) The one module with a clean PnL footprint is cost-awareness: removing it raises realized cost +10% (the execution pair +18%); the cost tier matters where modules do not (HIGH is 122× the LOW cost, vol 71%, DD -76%). (vii) Behavioral diagnostics -detaching modules degrades the process, not the outcome (Fig. 11). Stripping modules collapses decision scrutiny: the bare-workflow agent does half the analysis (research brief 0.51×), weighs half the signals (0.48×), scouts no candidates and performs no reflection (both 0.00×), spends 40% less reasoning effort, yet proposes the largest trades (intended move 1.23×). On the same round (2025-11-03) the full agent records a mean-variance optimization with explicit weights, exclusions, binding constraints and a cost-management lesson, while the bare-workflow agent's entire rationale is "Optimizer: risk_parity. Binding constraints: []. Accepted 0 adjustments" with no reflection (Appendix E) -premature construction, presumptuous intent, absent scrutiny. None of it shows in returns because the constrained construction contains it: concentration is flat (max-weight ~0.11, HHI ~0.09) across all thirteen, so the rising presumptuousness surfaces in proposed moves the caps clip, never in realized positions. The guardrails convert degraded decisions into safe outcomes in a benign regime; the behavior and capability axes record what the constraints mask.

(viii) Module feasibility for a professional agent-investing platform. Synthesising the returns / risk / cost / capability / behavioral evidence yields an actionable per-module verdict -the kind of guidance the instrument is built to produce (Table 10), not a returns rank. The synthesis is the paper's thesis in miniature: module value is real but lives off the returns axis -in risk discipline (intrinsic to the constraints), in cost, and in decision process (depth, scrutiny, learning, measured intent). A returns leaderboard sees none of it and would prune the lot; the instrument prices each module on the axis it actually moves, and tells a platform builder which modules to keep, why, and under what regime the verdict flips. (ix) The regime does much of the work -which masks both module value and model risk-taking. Every number above is measured in one benign, rising market: over the campaign SPY returned +27% with only a -8.9% drawdown and a calm VIX (median 17; above 25 on just 7% of days). Three consequences follow, and each is a reason the ablation ∆ are small. First, the market -not the modules -drives the returns: in a trending bull almost any reasonable long-only book posts a strong Sharpe and clears the defensive baselines, so removing a module cannot move returns much -there is little danger for the analytical or learning machinery to steer the agent away from. Second, the modules whose value is most regime-contingent are exactly the ones this period mutes: the information stack (news-sentiment / world-macro / asset-class-data) earns its keep at turning points -spotting deteriorating breadth or a regime shift -not while riding a trend; the learning loop (memory / reflection) pays off by adapting across regimes, and a single stable trend gives it little to adapt to; and the covariance-aware optimizer (advanced-quant) matters most when correlations spike in a sell-off, not when everything rises together. Their flat ablation ∆ here is therefore weak evidence of irrelevance and strong evidence that this regime cannot test them. Third -and most consequential -a rising market masks risk-taking shortcomings the scorecard catches but returns do not. In a bull run the configurations that look best on raw return are those that take the most risk (full exposure, momentum-chasing, concentration), while the prudent de-risking the agents actually exhibit (half the index's drawdown, Table 9) costs return and looks worse -so a returns leaderboard in this regime rewards exactly the recklessness a drawdown would punish and penalizes the risk management that would protect it. qwen3•structured's 5-round "Sharpe 9.82" ( §7.3) is the extreme: an artifact a bull-market returns ranking flatters and the Reliability / risk axes expose. The benign window is thus not merely a power limit on the ablations (stress bucket ≈ 4-5 of 26 rounds, §8.7) but a structural reason the capability and risk-adjusted axes are necessary -they are what stays diagnostic when the regime makes returns uninformative, or worse, misleading.

p.s: Methodology note: reasoning needs output headroom
p.t: A test-time-compute model can look like an incapable portfolio manager when it is merely truncated -a tight output cap severs its chain-of-thought mid-stream. We therefore standardize on a generous output budget and report cap-hit, truncation, rate-limit, and parse-fail as first-class reliability telemetry. Without that telemetry a benchmark misattributes a budget or infrastructure artifact (qwen3's incompletion, §7.5) to a capability gap -exactly the misread a returns-only or single-configuration view invites.

p.s: RQ7: Net of Costs, Agents Clear the Defensive Baselines but Not the Index Cleanly
p.t: Over the full bi-weekly year, the reliable structured configurations clear a median ~6 of 8 passive baselines (deepseek 6.3, haiku 6.0, gemini 5.7; Figure 12) -a materially stronger showing than the single-quarter design pilot, where no agent beat SPY. But the beaten set is dominated by the suite's defensive / diversified members (IEF bonds, risk-parity, 60/40, equal-weight); the cap-weighted equity index remains the hardest bar, and the autonomous configurations clear far fewer (gemini and haiku autonomous: just 1/8). The honest reading the instrument enforces -scoring every config against the whole suite, not a hand-picked benchmark -is that under realistic costs these agents reliably beat the defensive baselines but do not uniformly clear the cap-weighted index, and autonomy (autonomous mode) markedly weakens even that. (qwen3•structured's 8/8 is excluded as a 5-round artifact, §7.3.) The index gap is a de-risking trade, not a deficit. "Does not beat the cap-weighted index" understates what the risk-adjusted read shows in Table 9: against SPY the agents run lower volatility and roughly half the maximum drawdown (-4.1% vs -8.9%) at the same Sharpe and ≈2× the Calmar. The shortfall in absolute return is the price of deliberate diversification away from the index's mega-cap concentration -a trade that loses a little in a concentrated bull run and wins decisively in a drawdown. So the honest statement is not "no skill vs the index" but "a risk-managed profile the index does not have": the agents convert a passive long-only mandate into a lower-drawdown, comparable-Sharpe strategy, and -per the ablation diagnostics -this risk discipline is intrinsic to the constrained construction and survives even the bare-workflow stripping. The Composure axis ( §7.6) is the in-instrument measure of exactly this behavior; a returns leaderboard, fixated on the -2.4% vs SPY, would miss it.

On clean, chain-verified campaign data (5 models × 2 modes; repeated runs for the reliable models; a 13-configuration ablation grid; held-out judge) the instrument (i) discriminates decision quality where Sharpe conflates it -the capability leader (deepseek•structured, APM-CS 72.4) is not the Sharpe "winner" (qwen3•structured 9.82, exposed as a 5/26round artifact) (F1); (ii) explains outcomes through measurable deficits -qwen3's structured operational incompletion (truncation + rate-limiting) and gemini's persistent parse-fails (Reliability), the autonomous-mode Composure churn, and weak cohortwide Acuity (F3-F4); (iii) shows scaffold reshapes capability by model-specific amounts (deepseek +36 APM-CS, structured→autonomous) (F2); and (iv) surfaces benchmark limitations the campaign was built to expose -even repeated-run ablations cannot rank module value by returns (though the capability axes catch analysis-blind→Acuity), and the HIGH cost tier is mis-calibrated ( §7.7). No configuration dominates all five axes, so by the instrument's own standard the cohort is not cleanly rankable -the intended demonstration that this is an instrument, not a leaderboard.

Because every round stores the agent's stated analysis, rationale, reflection, and parse status, the trail lets us read behavior, not just scores -and the most instructive live behavior is an autonomous-mode convergence to hold (no rebalance) that, examined closely, decomposes into two distinct, model-specific mechanisms. The structured scaffold prevents both. Two roads to the same hold (Fig. 13). Across the nine live days, exactly two of six models ever produce a null-strategy hold, and only in autonomous mode: gemini-3.5-flash holds 6 of 9 rounds and minimax-m3 5 of 9, while the other four autonomous modelsand all six in structured mode -hold 0%. The two roads are distinct: -gemini-3.5-flash -tool-turn-budget exhaustion. Its reflection carries a complete mean-variance thesis (ten high-momentum names, a risk-on regime read), yet the committed round records only a truncation marker: the autonomous agent spends its tool-turn budget exploring and never serializes a final allocation, so an empty-weights fallback holds the book. It reasoned but did not deliver in budget. -minimax-m3 -governance-schema-adherence failure. The round is rejected for emitting schema-invalid output -an empty value where the output schema required a list -and with no valid decision it falls back to hold. (Held rounds even carry longer rationales: the model produces more text, but malformed.) Intermittent, independent, recoverable -not a one-way collapse. The first live week reads like a clean "day-1 trade, then lock-up": both models traded day 1 and then held days 2-4 in lockstep, which a short pilot would report as a deterministic day-2 collapse. The second week overturns that reading. The holds are intermittent (both models trade on several later days -gemini on 06-23/06-24, minimax on 06-23/06-25/06-26 -so the failure is recoverable, not absorbing), and they are independent: in week 2 the two models hold on different days (06-24 minimax holds while gemini trades; 06-25/06-26 gemini holds while minimax trades), with no synchrony. The diagnostically correct summary is therefore a per-model autonomous hold-rate (gemini 0.67, minimax 0.56) driven by a stochastic, model-specific fragility the autonomous scaffold exposes -not a shared, monotone "models stop trading after day 1."
