This is exactly the kind of claim a longer live horizon is needed to get right, and a caution against over-reading any few-round live result, our own week-1 pilot included. Scaffold magnifies vs. constrains (the structured-autonomous thread). The same minimax-m3 in structured mode still logs parse failures yet keeps trading: the staged pipeline (Risk-Officer review, MAPC reconciliation) contains a malformed sub-output and recovers, where the single-shot autonomous path lets the same failure collapse the whole round. This is a concrete instance of a recurring theme -structure converts a model's raw fragility into graceful degradation, at the cost of the autonomy that, for the more capable models, yields the cohort's best decisions (claude-sonnet-4.6 and qwen3.7-plus both score markedly higher autonomous than structured -69.1 vs 52.7 and 61.8 vs 41.8 -and deepseek-v4-pro scores equally in both). Whether an agent is best deployed as a disciplined expert-human proxy (structured) or given autonomy to exceed human heuristics is therefore model-dependent, not settled -a question we return to in §8.

Competence, read fairly. The trail is not only a catalogue of failure modes. claudesonnet-4.6's day-1 rationale is crisp and executable: it reads a risk-on regime (VIX ~18), flags a negative momentum loading in its factor model and rotates to correct it, and exits its worst-momentum, highest-volatility names -a defensible thesis that the allocation then follows, and the scorecard rewards it (Coherence 0.57, APM-CS 69.1 -the live leader). The same field that exposes minimax's schema failure credits claude's discipline; that even-handedness is the point of reading the trail. Every quote above is pinned to a hash-verified round_id (anecdote bank, Appendix E). A re-run does not remove these holds -they are deterministic consequences of each model's behavior under the autonomous scaffold, not transient errors -so we report them as characteristics, not bugs, and exclude null-strategy rounds from the consistency axis (the scorer flags them explicitly). Each maps back to a capability axis (e.g., 1→Coherence, 4→Acuity, 6→Reliability), so the qualitative read explains, in the model's own words and actions, how the quantitative deficits arise. A fuller per-model behavioral table (clip-rate, RO-override rate, mean tool-turns, lessons/round, retry-rate) is a natural extension of this trail; here we report the most diagnostic slice -the hold-mechanism split (Figure 13) and the anecdote bank (Appendix E) -and leave the exhaustive tabulation to future work.

The campaign makes the central argument concretely: the capability leader (deepseek•structured, APM-CS 72.4) and the nominal Sharpe "winner" (qwen3•structured, 9.82) are different configurations -and the latter is a 5-of-26-round artifact (Reliability 0.19) the scorecard exposes rather than crowns. A leaderboard would report a spurious number and stop; the scorecard instead returns a profile for each -qwen3 attends to the noise distractor over the alpha signal (negative Acuity) and cannot sustain the structured pipeline (null PM responses from truncation + provider rate-limiting -operational, not cognitive, §7.5); haiku•structured posts the best reliable Sharpe (3.20) yet the lowest Coherence (0.15); deepseek leads on balance but is only mid-pack on Sharpe; and the same model's profile shifts sharply with scaffold (deepseek 72.4 structured → 36.7 autonomous). These are research-actionable statements (where to intervene), not a rank. They also explain why we decline to rank: no configuration dominates all five axes, and a credible cross-regime ranking would need an order of magnitude more models, regimes, and repeated runs -out of scope by design, and exactly the larger evidence base the instrument is meant to support over time.

p.s: Capability Axes as General Agent Diagnostics
p.t: Each axis is deliberately a finance instantiation of a general capability, which lets trading findings speak to model behavior at large. Coherence is systems-level reasoning vs. greedy local moves -the gap between an agent's stated analysis and its action; the judge/agreement divergence ( §5.5) is a finance reading of "the model can name the right consideration but does not let it govern the output." Read through Anderson's ACT* lens [25], this is a declarative→procedural deficit: the agent holds the declarative knowledge (it states the correct consideration -"VIX is elevated, reduce momentum exposure") but lacks the compiled procedural production rule that would convert that knowledge into the specific weights -exactly the failure ACT* predicts for knowledge acquired from text without compilation through practice. On this reading the coherence gap, near-invariant across backtest and live (+0.33 / +0.34), is -as the most parsimonious interpretation we offer, not a tested causal claim -consistent with the deficit rather than measurement noise: the declarative store transfers cleanly to new data (the agent still names the right factors) while the missing procedural compilation transfers too (the actions still do not follow), so the gap reproduces at the same magnitude on data the models never saw. The reflect-and-learn loop (the ALE stage and three-tier memory, §3.6) is then the mechanism by which a benchmark could, in principle, supply the practice ACT* says is requiredmaking the memory ablation ( §7.7) a direct test of whether in-context experience can begin to compile the missing rules. Acuity is salience attention under polluted contextthe negative-Acuity autonomous run is a finance reading of distractibility amid abundant, partly misleading data. Composure is robustness to perturbation vs. overcorrectiongemini-autonomous's vol-driven churn ( §7.6) is reactive overcorrection. Discipline is systematic alignment to a standing mandate vs. turn-by-turn instruction-followingself-regulation without a hard guardrail. Reliability is protocol/format adherence and operational robustness -completing a structured tool-use task in valid form, every time. Read this way, the scorecard is a portable lens: the same five questions can be asked of any agentic system operating a complex, cost-bearing, partially observable process.

p.s: Capability Axes as General Agent Diagnostics
p.t: Parallels in the benchmark literature. Three of CLQT's findings rhyme with results obtained by very different instruments, which is mild evidence they are properties of the agents, not of our setup. First, the coherence gap echoes Profit Mirage [8]: where they show apparent alpha collapses once leakage is removed, we show apparent skill fails to cohere with stated reasoning -both are cases of a headline number evaporating under a closer look, and both argue for measuring the process rather than trusting the outcome. Second, the capability ̸ = outcome result (the Sharpe "winner" is a 5-round artifact, §7.3) is the portfolio-management instance of procedure-aware evaluation's "corrupt success" [12] -task success reached through an unsound process -which CLQT surfaces because the audit trail scores the process, not just the PnL. Third, the repeated-run noise floor ( §7.7) is a concrete instance of the statistical-power cautions that agent-evaluation surveys raise in the abstract: a single-axis, single-run score is not just incomplete but unstable, which is why CLQT reports a profile, bounds module-importance with a repeated-run protocol, and treats reliability as a first-class axis.

p.s: Scaffolding × Capability, and the Cost of Intelligence
p.t: The structured↔autonomous contrast is the clearest interaction in the campaign: structure lifts the capability profile broadly (Composure, Discipline) -most dramatically for deepseek (APM-CS +36) -but it also demands a governance schema that stresses the smaller models in different ways (gemini's genuine parse-fails; qwen3's operational truncation + rate-limiting, §7.5). Structure thus helps and hurts the same model on different axes -and, for deepseek, reverses with mode (reliable structured, less reliable autonomous) -a more useful statement than "scaffolding helps weaker models," and one only a multi-axis read can make. The efficiency ledger sharpens it: gemini•structured is by far the heaviest reasoner (~275k reasoning tokens/run despite thinking being pinned off), its compute consumed by the retry loop around its schema failures. "Cost of intelligence" here is dominated by failed reasoning, not productive reasoning (Figure 14). Which investment schema -structured, autonomous, or hybrid? The live week sharpens the structured↔autonomous contrast into a design choice. Structure acts as a containment layer: it converts a model's raw fragility into graceful degradation (minimax-m3 keeps trading in structured mode but collapses to holds when autonomous, §7.11) and lifts Composure and Discipline broadly. Autonomy removes that scaffolding -which penalizes models that cannot self-govern (gemini-3.5-flash, minimax-m3) yet rewards the more capable ones: claude-sonnet-4.6 scores higher autonomous than structured, and deepseek-v4-pro scores equally in both modes. The implication is that the right schema is model-dependent, and the interesting frontier is neither pole but a hybrid -let an agent operate autonomously while a lightweight governance layer (schema validation, mandate reconciliation, a held-out coherence check) catches exactly the failure modes structure would have prevented, keeping the upside of autonomy without its brittleness. Whether an LLM is best deployed as a disciplined expert-human proxy (structured) or trusted to exceed human heuristics (autonomous) is therefore not a single answer but a function of the model's self-governance capability -which the scorecard measures directly. We pose this as an open, evidence-informed question rather than a prescription; settling it is a natural use of the instrument as the model panel and the live horizon grow.

The output-budget finding ( §7.8) is a methodological warning for the field: a reasoning model under a tight output cap can look like an incapable portfolio manager when it is merely a truncated one. The fix is operationally simple (budget generously; billing is on generated tokens) and the telemetry is mandatory (cap-hits, truncation, parse-fail). A benchmark that does not separate these will misattribute a budget artifact to model capability -the exact error the truncation / rate-limit telemetry corrects (qwen3's incompletion, §7.5).

The cost-tier ablation surfaced its own measurement bug: the HIGH (Almgren-Chriss) tier charges an implausible ~+527 bps/round, so it is mis-calibrated, not "pessimistic." We therefore keep LOW (calibrated against the live broker paper fills, §5.2) and treat HIGHtier recalibration as future work -an example of the instrument auditing itself. The tamper-evident hash chain ( §4.4) underwrites all of this: because verification recomputes hashes and checks prev-round linkage, the numbers in §7 are not merely reported as coming from those runs -a third party with the persisted store can prove it.

p.s: Behavioral Interpretability from the Audit Trail
p.t: Because every decision artifact is persisted and hash-chained, CLQT supports a qualitative, reproducible read of how models reason and behave (method §6.5; results §7.11) -intent-vs-clip gaps, Risk-Officer negotiations, tool-foraging order, and lesson formation/reuse, each anecdote resolving to a hash-verified round. We frame this as behavior plus self-report, not hidden chain-of-thought, complementary to the axes: the axes quantify where a configuration fails; the behavioral read explains, in the model's own words and actions, how. We regard it as a primary use of the audit trail, not a side effect.

We read this single-period campaign through the standard threats-to-validity frame: what the design can identify, what its constructs assume, and the conditions under which its conclusions hold. • What returns can identify. By construction the returns axis is underpowered to attribute module value at this scale: every single-module and cluster knockout lands inside the ±0.42 repeated-run band ( §7.7), so no module-importance claim can rest on returns -we read the flat ∆Sharpe as a statement about the metric, not the modules, and confine module value to the capability axes (where, e.g., analysis-blind drives Acuity to 0.02). Two related scope conditions: the HIGH cost tier is mis-calibrated (~527 bps/round; LOW retained), and Acuity and Discipline are mode-confounded, so they are read only within mode. • Construct validity of the axes. The five axes operationalize latent capabilities, and the v2 hardening of Discipline and Composure shows the read is sensitive to how those constructs are defined. We argue construct validity empirically rather than assume it -rank-stability across the revision (τ = 0.78, ρ = 0.90), near-orthogonality (mean |r| = 0.28), and robustness to leave-one-out and judgereweighting (Appendix F) -and note candidly that the revision overturned one prior sub-finding (memory "breaking" Composure was an artifact of the earlier construction). • Judge independence. A held-out, non-cohort judge mitigates but cannot fully eliminate LLM-as-judge self-preference. A second, different-family judge corroborates the headline gap (GLM-5.2, ρ = 0.65; +0.28/+0.34 vs +0.33/+0.34), yet minimax-m3 also sits in the live cohort, so its own live rounds are self-adjudicated -it rates itself among the lowest (no inflation), but a fully clean design would draw the judge from outside both panels (Appendix C, Table C1).

• External validity: one regime, modeled backtest costs. The window is a single, predominantly rising market (SPY +27%, max DD -8.9%, VIX median 17), and backtest costs are modeled rather than executed (the live track supplies real fills on the daily deltas). This bounds every returns-based statement to one regime, and the bound cuts both ways: the benign window masks the modules whose value concentrates at turning points and flatters high-exposure risk-taking while penalizing the prudent de-risking the agents exhibit ( §7.7). The capability and risk-adjusted axes are comparatively regime-robust, but absolute-return conclusions should be read as regime-conditional. • Live evidence: consistency, not transfer. The live track shows the instrument measures the same decision property on genuinely unseen data, not that any specific model generalizes -the live and backtest cohorts are different model versions, and live returns are indicative-only by design (daily flatten; overnight exposure is virtual and modeled). The short horizon keeps Acuity and Composure the shortest-baseline axes; tellingly, the second live week overturned two week-1 reads and converted an apparent day-2 hold "collapse" into an intermittent, recoverable rate ( §7.11) -itself a caution against over-reading any short live record, ours included. None of these undercut the contribution -the instrument and its read-out -but all bound what the numbers may claim.

The instrument is built to be populated over time; the priorities are the dimensions along which this paper's reading is thinnest, not a longer list of run parameters. • Scale and statistical power. Broaden the model panel and the number of repeated runs so every axis carries confidence intervals and rank-stability rather than point estimates and run-ranges -turning the current map into one with quantified uncertainty. • Regime robustness. This campaign sat in a single benign, rising market. Stratifying rounds by market regime and reporting how far each capability degrades from calm into stress is the load-bearing extension before any returns-based conclusion can generalize. • Generalization of the profile. Varying the standing mandate and the reasoningeffort budget tests whether a model's capability fingerprint is a stable property or an artifact of the single mandate and effort level used here. • Active stress and instrument hardening. Adversarial misleading-data and canary probes would stress Acuity and Composure directly rather than relying on naturally-occurring noise; a broader held-out judge panel, a recalibrated HIGH cost tier, and a judge drawn from outside the live cohort would further harden the measurement itself. Finer-grained per-sector and per-name attribution is a natural next layer, letting the same audit trail localize not only where a process fails but on which exposures.

CLQT is a closed-loop, cost-aware, temporally-gated benchmark whose purpose is diagnostic: its tamper-evident audit trail and five-axis capability scorecard characterize how LLM agents reason and behave in autonomous portfolio management -surfacing competencies, limitations, and unanticipated behaviors alike -rather than ranking them by a single quarter's return. On a chain-verified year-long bi-weekly campaign (5 models × 2 modes, repeated runs for the reliable models, a 13-configuration ablation grid, a held-out judge, and a live broker track) the instrument cleanly separates outcome from capabilitythe capability leader (deepseek•structured) is not the nominal Sharpe winner (exposed as a 5-of-26-round qwen3 artifact), and no configuration dominates all five axes -surfaces model-specific limitations (structured governance-schema adherence) invisible to returns, exposes mode-specific stability characteristics (volatility-driven churn) and a cohortwide coherence weakness an independent judge reveals, and even audits its own cost model. Adding a two-week live broker paper-trading track (nine valid days), we show the instrument transfers to genuinely unseen data: the signal-action-agreement↔judge coherence gap is essentially the same on backtest and live (+0.33 / +0.34), and the live track exposes an autonomous-only hold behavior -an intermittent, recoverable, per-model hold-rate decomposing into two distinct model-specific mechanisms (tool-turn exhaustion vs schema-adherence failure) the structured scaffold prevents. We deliberately decline to rank: a credible ranking needs an order of magnitude more models and regimes than any single study affords, and the lasting contribution of a benchmark is the reusable map of limitations it produces. Broader repeated-run, regime-stratified campaigns can populate that map further; this paper establishes the instrument that draws it.
